extracted.intended_audience: general readers / students of 19th-century literary prose (readers of De Quincey and retellings of Indian folktales)
extracted.subtask_description: A literary excerpt (De Quincey) retelling Indian folktales and moral parables; contains narrative plus embedded prescriptive/pedagogic statements about education, selection of teachers, discipline, and pseudo-scientific demonstration. Useful for literary analysis or extracting embedded normative guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parental methods of upbringing (pedagogy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The father sedulously cultivated implicit obedience, humble respect, warm attachment, and virtues; he praised secretly and reprehended openly; derided their looks and dressed them coarsely; punctually disappointed treats; revoked promises (without breaking his word) to enforce discipline; frequently threatened, browbeat, and overawed them with the rod and the tongue, with the terrors of this world, and with the horrors of the next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as an intentional education strategy: praise in private, public reprimand, enforced austerity of dress and diet, calculated disappointments, and the use of fear as a motivating force. The passage frames these as recommendations drawn from 'all the best works upon education' (i.e., conventional pedagogy of the narrator's culture) and as measures to prevent vanity and enforce humility.

rubrics_metrics.name: School daily schedule and study regimen
rubrics_metrics.description: At age six they were transferred to the Chatushpati (school). Every morning teacher and pupils assembled; they laboured till noon, had only two hours (for bathing, eating, sleep, and worship), resumed at 3 P.M. until twilight, then worshipped, ate and drank for an hour, and returned to study, repeating the day's lessons, till 10 P.M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A highly regimented schedule: intensive study in morning and evening, short mid-day respite, compulsory worship breaks, and late-evening revision. Use of strict hours and repetitive memorization (recitation and repeating lessons) is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leisure and conduct prohibitions for pupils
rubrics_metrics.description: In rare days of ease pupils were enjoined: not to engage in night frolics; not to use free jests or light expressions; not to draw pictures on walls; not to eat honey, flesh, and sweet substances turned acid; not to talk to little girls at the well-side; on no account to wear sandals, carry an umbrella, or handle a die even for love; and by no means to steal their neighbours' mangoes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of specific behavioral prohibitions intended to preserve decorum and guard against moral laxity; these function as concrete discipline rules and anti-patterns for pupils' leisure activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum emphasis and exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Their attention during work time was unremittingly directed to the Vedas. Worldly studies were almost excluded; when worldly subjects appeared they were so ill-treated they 'well nigh lost all form and feature.' History became 'The Annals of India on Brahminical Principles'; geography 'The Lands of the Vedas'; law 'The Institutes of Manu.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explicit curricular bias toward sacred/religious texts and traditional Brahminical viewpoints, with worldly or secular subjects marginalized or reframed to fit the sacred canon. This prescribes content selection and epistemic framing for instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age milestones and expected attainments
rubrics_metrics.description: At age four they had read a variety of hymns and spiritual songs; by six they entered Chatushpati; at twelve they were formally entered at the University of Kasi (after which different moral outcomes occur).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies expected ages for stages of religious/academic formation and the kinds of accomplishments (memorization of prayers, entrance to formal schooling and university) associated with each stage; useful as a timeline for educational progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of moral characters
rubrics_metrics.description: There are four different characters: (1) he who perfectly obeys commands; (2) he who practices the commands but follows evil; (3) he who does neither good nor evil (also an offender for neglect); and (4) he who does nothing but evil. The four youths belong to the fourth category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A moral-evaluative typology used to judge persons' conduct; the rubric both categorizes behavior and justifies differential treatment (discipline, expulsion) based on category placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: University disciplinary measures and recommended sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: For gamblers: 'Cut off the gambler’s nose and ears, hold up his name to public contempt, and drive him out of the country...'; for libertines: shunning women, expulsion from the seat of learning; for thieves: petty larceny punishable with fine, theft with mutilation of the hand, robbery with loss of life; specific gradation for cutting purses (first penalty chopping off the fingers, second loss of the hand, third death).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This passage outlines graduated, severe judicial/disciplinary penalties as official recommendations to deter vice and maintain institutional honor. It exemplifies administrative policy (punitive and exclusionary measures) tied to specific offences and carries moralizing justification (example to others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for a Guru/teacher
rubrics_metrics.description: They chose a Guru 'strictly according to the orders of their faith': a wise man of honourable family and affable demeanour, who was not a glutton nor leprous, nor blind of one eye, nor blind of both eyes, nor very short, nor suffering from whitlows, asthma, or other disease, nor noisy and talkative, nor with any defect about the fingers and toes, nor subject to his wife.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete positive and negative selection attributes for a spiritual/academic teacher: emphasis on moral character, family status, affability, and absence of certain physical ailments or social defects. These operate as eligibility criteria and anti-patterns for candidate selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of economic sanctions to motivate reform
rubrics_metrics.description: The father stopped their monthly allowance and added that if they repaired to the neighbouring university of Jayasthal and showed themselves better, he would have their maternal uncle supply necessities. He intended monetary withdrawal plus conditional support as motive for reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes removing financial support and coupling it with conditional pathways to assistance (reform at another institution) as a means to compel behavioral change; an example of remedial policy combining sanction and conditional aid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform pathway: exile to another university
rubrics_metrics.description: The youths were to 'immediately exchange this university for a country life' or 'repair to the neighbouring university of Jayasthal' to 'show themselves something better'—a prescribed remedial relocation and probationary education elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional remediation consists of expulsion from the present setting and supervised exposure to another educational environment deemed more practical or reformative; serves as corrective policy rather than purely punitive action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public demonstration protocol for alleged life-restoring science
rubrics_metrics.description: For the vivification demonstration the operators: spread the bones upon the ground and fixed each one into its proper socket (including teeth and tusks); connected the skeleton with the muscles and heart of an elephant; fitted in brain and eyes of a tom-cat; covered the body with the hide of a young rhinoceros; and the atheist produced 'a globule having another globule within itself.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stepwise, quasi-procedural list (bones assembly, muscular/heart grafting, brain/eye insertion, hide covering, and introducing a 'globule within a globule') for effecting a reanimation spectacle. Presented as the technical recipe for the experiment and implicitly as an evidentiary protocol to convince an audience (ocular demonstration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Community evaluation of novel scientific claims (implicit standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two learned bodies react differently: Gaurians deride the new invention as impious, Jayasthalians hail it; the Jayasthalians argue 'if erroneous, it will necessarily sink into oblivion; if real, it will tend only to instruct and to enlighten the world.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An implicit epistemic rubric for assessing scientific novelty: allow claims to stand or fall by evidence and subsequent practical demonstration, but recognize that sociocultural biases (prejudice, over-eagerness, or derision) will shape reception. Use public demonstration and reproducibility to adjudicate truth claims.
